description: Bug report from a user of python-semver: checking Version.parse("2.0.0") == {} in our config loader crashes with TypeError: Version.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'major', coming from inside the library. Find the problem and fix it. Change src/semver/ only.
environment: Python >= 3.13 stdlib; base tree = python-semver 0aa17a3^ (src, tests, LICENSE.txt, pyproject, README, .gitignore; two test symlinks into docs/ removed) plus the task-owned helper bench_fixtures/ops.py, no repository history; the project's own test suite needs pytest, which is not installed
visible_checks: python -W ignore -c "from src.semver import Version; print(Version.parse('1.2.3') < (2, 0, 0))" (from the workspace root; pytest is not available)
provenance: real fix: python-semver commit 0aa17a3 (Handle malformed collection operands in Version comparisons, #479, 2026-09-12); reference/good.patch is that commit's src diff; symptom-only description (== with an empty dict crashes); hidden cases authored for agent-benchmark (2026-10-12): Python's data-model rule for unsupported operands (== False, != True, ordering raises TypeError) that the report does not state, plus guards; cases run through the task-owned helper bench_fixtures/ops.py; other reference patches built by build_task.py. Public repository: contamination possible; v2 (2026-10-12, after a calibration in which both agents failed the same cases): cases with non-numeric list parts were removed, because they raise ValueError like an invalid version string, which the library keeps raising, so treating them alike was a defensible reading
